title.en: Volume 108 Book of Later Jin 10: Biographies 5 - Li Song, Su Fengji, Li Lin, Long Min, Liu Ding, Zhang Yun, Ren Yanhao
title.raw: 卷一百〇八 漢書10: 列傳五 李崧 蘇逢吉 李鏻 龍敏 劉鼎 張允 任延皓 Volume 108 Book of Later Jin 10: Biographies 5 - Li Song, Su Fengji, Li Lin, Long Min, Liu Ding, Zhang Yun, Ren Yanhao

sentences.zh: 李崧，深州饒陽人。

translations.literal: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song was from Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父舜卿，本州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Shunqing was registrar of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Shunqing, served as the prefectural registrar.

sentences.zh: 崧幼而聰敏，十餘歲為文，家人奇之。

translations.literal: Song was clever in youth; by his teens he could write, and his family marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Song was bright as a boy, and by his early teens he could already compose prose, to his family's astonishment.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，本府署為參軍。

translations.literal: At his coming of age, the prefectural office appointed him adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached manhood, the prefectural command appointed him as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 其父嘗謂宗人李鏻曰：「大醜生處，形奇氣異，前途應不居徒勞之地，賴吾兄誨激之。

translations.literal: His father once said to his clansman Li Lin: "Where Big Ugly was born, his form was strange and his spirit unusual; his future should not be spent in vain toil—he will rely on my elder brother to instruct and spur him."
translations.idiomatic: His father once told his kinsman Li Lin, "Big Ugly was born under an odd star—his bearing is unusual and his spirit distinctive. He is not meant to waste his life in drudgery; he will need my elder brother's teaching to drive him forward."

sentences.zh: 」大醜即崧之小字也。

translations.literal: " Big Ugly was Song's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: " Big Ugly was Song's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 同光初，魏王繼岌為興聖宮使，兼領鎮州節鉞，崧以參軍從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, the Prince of Wei, Jiji, was commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the military commission of Zhen Prefecture; Song followed as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang reign, Prince Jiji of Wei served as commissioner of the Xingsheng Palace while also holding the Zhenzhou command; Song accompanied him as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 時推官李蕘掌書，崧見其起草不工，密謂掌事呂柔曰：「令公皇子，天下瞻望，至於尺牘往來，章表論列，稍須文理合宜。

translations.literal: At the time the investigating censor Li Rao handled documents; Song saw that his drafts were unskilled and secretly told the steward Lu Rou: "His Lordship is the Emperor's son, and the realm looks to him; as for letters exchanged and memorials argued, they ought at least to be literate and fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The investigating censor Li Rao was then in charge of correspondence. Song found his drafts clumsy and quietly told the steward Lu Rou, "The Prince is the Emperor's son—the whole realm watches him. Every note that goes out and every memorial he submits ought to read with some polish and propriety."

sentences.zh: 李侍御起草，未能盡善。

translations.literal: Censor Li's drafts are not fully adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li's drafts are not quite up to the mark.

sentences.zh: 」呂曰：「公試代為之。

translations.literal: " Lu said, "Sir, try drafting them yourself."
translations.idiomatic: " Lu replied, "Why don't you try drafting them yourself?"

sentences.zh: 」呂得崧所作，示盧質、馮道，皆稱之。

translations.literal: " Lu obtained what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao; both praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " Lu took Song's drafts to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao, and both praised them highly.

sentences.zh: 繇是擢為興聖宮巡官，獨掌奏記。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and alone handled memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Song was then promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and given sole charge of memorials.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入洛，授太常寺協律郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, he was appointed harmonizing officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhuangzong took Luoyang, Song was appointed harmonizing officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 王師伐蜀，繼岌為都統，以崧掌書記。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song was made chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial forces marched on Shu, Jiji served as overall commander and Song became his chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，樞密使郭崇韜為宦官誣構，繼岌遂殺崇韜父子，外尚未知。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao was framed by eunuchs; Jiji then killed Chongtao and his son, while the outside still did not know.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu fell, eunuchs framed Commissioner Guo Chongtao, and Jiji executed Chongtao and his son before word reached the outside world.

sentences.zh: 崧白繼岌曰：「王何為作此危事？

translations.literal: Song told Jiji: "Prince, why do such a perilous deed?"
translations.idiomatic: Song said to Jiji, "Your Highness, why commit such a reckless act?"

sentences.zh: 至於不容崇韜，至洛誅之未晚。

translations.literal: As for not tolerating Chongtao, to execute him at Luoyang would not be late.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Chongtao could not be tolerated, it would not be too late to execute him once you reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今懸軍五千里，無咫尺書詔，便殺重臣，非謀也。

translations.literal: Now the army is suspended five thousand li away, without an inch of written edict, yet a great minister is killed—this is no plan.
translations.idiomatic: You have an army stranded five thousand li from home, with not a line of imperial writ to authorize it, and you kill a great minister—that is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌曰：「吾亦悔之。

translations.literal: " Jiji said, "I too regret it."
translations.idiomatic: " Jiji said, "I regret it as well."

sentences.zh: 」崧召書吏三四人，登樓去梯，取黃紙矯寫詔書，倒使都統印發之。

translations.literal: " Song summoned three or four clerks, went upstairs and removed the ladder, took yellow paper and forged an edict, and had the overall commander's seal impressed upside down to issue it.
translations.idiomatic: " Song called three or four clerks upstairs, had the ladder pulled away, drafted an edict on yellow paper under the Prince's name, and issued it with the overall commander's seal impressed in reverse.

sentences.zh: 翌日，告諸軍，軍情稍定。

translations.literal: The next day he announced it to the armies, and army sentiment gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he announced the edict to the troops, and morale gradually steadied.

sentences.zh: 及自蜀還，明宗革命，任圜以宰相判三司，用崧為鹽鐵推官，賜緋。

translations.literal: When he returned from Shu, Emperor Mingzong took power; Ren Huan as chancellor oversaw the Three Commissions and employed Song as salt-and-iron investigating officer, granting scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shu campaign, when Emperor Mingzong seized the throne, Chancellor Ren Huan, who oversaw the Three Commissions, appointed Song salt-and-iron investigating officer and granted him scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 服闋，鎮帥範延光奏署掌書記。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, the military governor Fan Yanguang memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period, Military Governor Fan Yanguang recommended him as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 延光為樞密使，拜拾遺，直樞密院，遷補闕、起居郎、尚書郎，充職如故。

translations.literal: When Yanguang became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Song was made remonstrance official, assigned to the Bureau, and promoted through remonstrance supplementer, attendant of the bedchamber, and secretariat officer while continuing his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Yanguang became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Song was appointed remonstrance official and attached to the Bureau. He rose through remonstrance supplementer, attendant of the bedchamber, and secretariat officer while keeping his secretarial post.

sentences.zh: 長興末，改翰林學士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he was changed to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Changxing reign he was made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，拜端明殿學士、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai reign he was made Duanming Hall academician and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 先是，長興三年冬，契丹入雲中，朝廷欲命重將鎮太原。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the winter of the third year of Changxing, the Khitan entered Yunzhong; the court wished to appoint a weighty general to secure Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the winter of the third year of Changxing, the Khitan invaded Yunzhong, and the court sought a senior general to hold Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時晉祖為六軍副使，以秦王從榮不軌，懇求外任，深有北門之望，而大臣以晉高祖方權兵柄，難以議之。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin Ancestor was deputy commander of the Six Armies; because Prince Qin Congrong was unruly, he earnestly sought an outside post and deeply hoped for the northern gate, yet the great ministers, since the Jin Founder already held military power, found it hard to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The future Jin Founder was then deputy commander of the Six Armies. With Prince Congrong of Qin plotting rebellion, he urgently sought a post away from court and clearly coveted command of Taiyuan, but the senior ministers hesitated to propose him while he already wielded so much military authority.

sentences.zh: 一日，明宗怒其未奏，範延光、趙延壽等無對，退歸本院，共議其事，方欲以康義誠為之。

translations.literal: One day Emperor Mingzong was angry that they had not memorialized; Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and others had no reply; they withdrew to their bureau and jointly discussed the matter, and were just about to appoint Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Emperor grew angry that no recommendation had been submitted. Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and the others had no answer. They withdrew to the Bureau of Military Affairs to deliberate and were on the verge of naming Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 時崧最在下位，聳立請曰：「朝廷重兵多在北邊，須以重臣為帥，以某所見，非石太尉不可也。

translations.literal: At the time Song was lowest in rank; he stood erect and requested: "The court's heavy forces are mostly on the northern frontier; a weighty minister must be commander—in my view none but Grand Marshal Shi will do."
translations.idiomatic: Song, then the junior man present, rose and said, "Most of the empire's main forces lie on the northern frontier. We need a senior minister as commander—and in my view only Grand Marshal Shi will do."

sentences.zh: 」會明宗令中使促之，眾乃從其議。

translations.literal: " Just then Emperor Mingzong ordered a palace envoy to press them, and the assembly then followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " At that moment the Emperor sent a palace envoy to hurry them along, and the group adopted Song's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 翌日，晉祖既受太原之命，使心腹達意於崧云：「壘浮圖須與合卻尖。

translations.literal: The next day, after the Jin Ancestor had received the Taiyuan appointment, he sent a confidant to convey his meaning to Song: "When piling a pagoda, the spire must be fitted together."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, after receiving the Taiyuan command, the Jin Founder sent a confidant to tell Song, "When you raise a pagoda, the capstone must be set in place."—meaning Song had completed what he had begun.

sentences.zh: 」蓋感之深也。

translations.literal: " Such was the depth of his gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: " He was profoundly grateful.

sentences.zh: 及清泰末，晉祖入洛，崧與呂琦俱竄匿於伊闕民家。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, when the Jin Ancestor entered Luoyang, Song and Lü Qi both hid in a commoner's house at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai, when the Jin Founder marched into Luoyang, Song and Lü Qi went into hiding in a farmhouse at Yique.

sentences.zh: 旬日，晉高祖召為戶部侍郎，判戶部。

translations.literal: Within ten days Emperor Gaozu of Jin summoned him as vice minister of revenue and put him in charge of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Emperor Gaozu of Jin recalled him as Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜中書侍郎、同平章事，與桑維翰並兼樞密使。

translations.literal: After a month he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and fellow Grand Councillor, and together with Sang Weihan concurrently served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, sharing with Sang Weihan the concurrent post of military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 維翰鎮相州，未幾，廢樞密院，事歸中書，加尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Weihan secured Xiang Prefecture; before long the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished and affairs returned to the Secretariat; Song was given the additional title of right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan took command at Xiangzhou. Soon afterward the Bureau of Military Affairs was abolished and its duties returned to the Secretariat, and Song was further promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從幸鄴，丁外艱，恩制起復，崧上章數四，懇辭其命，優詔不允。

translations.literal: Accompanying the court to Ye, he entered mourning for his father; by gracious edict he was recalled to service; Song submitted several memorials earnestly declining the appointment, but gracious edicts did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the court at Ye he mourned his father. An edict recalled him to office, but Song submitted several memorials pleading to be excused; gracious replies refused him.

sentences.zh: 復上章，不報，崧不得已而視事。

translations.literal: He submitted again and received no reply; Song had no choice but to take up duties.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again without response and at last resumed office against his will.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，復用桑維翰為樞密使，命崧兼判三司。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, Sang Weihan was again used as commissioner of military affairs, and Song was ordered to oversee the Three Commissions concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: After the Young Emperor of Jin succeeded, Sang Weihan was restored as military affairs commissioner and Song was ordered to oversee the Three Commissions as well.

sentences.zh: 未幾，代維翰為樞密使，與馮玉對掌機密。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Weihan as commissioner and with Feng Yu jointly held the secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he replaced Weihan as commissioner and shared control of state secrets with Feng Yu.

sentences.zh: 開運末，崧、玉信契丹之詐，經略瀛、鄭，中渡之敗，落其奸謀。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, Song and Yu trusted the Khitan's deceit and planned Ying and Zheng; the defeat at Zhongdu exposed their treacherous scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyun, Song and Yu fell for Khitan deception in their operations around Ying and Zheng; the rout at Zhongdu laid bare the enemy's plot.

sentences.zh: 契丹入京師，趙延壽、張礪素稱崧之才，契丹主善遇之，以崧為太子太師，充樞密使。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the capital, Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li had long praised Song's talent; the Khitan ruler treated him well, making Song Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and filling the post of military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital, Zhao Yanshou and Zhang Li, who had long praised Song's ability, secured him favorable treatment. The Khitan ruler made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹主嘗謂左右曰：「我破南朝，只得李崧一人而已。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler once told those around him: "In breaking the Southern Court I gained only Li Song."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler once told his attendants, "In conquering the Southern Court I gained only one man worth having—Li Song."

sentences.zh: 」從契丹北行，留於鎮州。

translations.literal: " Following the Khitan northward, he was left at Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Khitan withdrew north, Song was left behind at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖平汴、洛，乃以崧之居第賜蘇逢吉，第中宿藏之物，皆為逢吉所有。

translations.literal: When Gaozu pacified Bian and Luo, he bestowed Song's residence on Su Fengji, and all goods stored in the house became Fengji's.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu secured Bianliang and Luoyang, he gave Song's mansion to Su Fengji, along with everything Song had stored there.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，鎮州逐麻答，崧與馮道、和凝十數人歸闕，授太子太傅。

translations.literal: That autumn Zhen Prefecture drove out Maduo; Song with Feng Dao, He Ning, and more than ten others returned to court and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhenzhou expelled the Khitan governor Maduo. Song returned to court with Feng Dao, He Ning, and a dozen others and was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崧對朝之權右，謙挹承顏，未嘗忤旨。

translations.literal: Facing the court's powerful, Song was modest and deferential in bearing and never went against the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: Before the powerful at court he was humble and obliging and never crossed the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘗以宅券獻蘇逢吉，不悅。

translations.literal: He once presented the deed of the house to Su Fengji, who was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He once offered Su Fengji the deed to his former house, to Fengji's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 崧二弟嶼、㠖，酣酒無識，與楊邠、蘇逢吉子弟杯酒之間，時言及奪我居第，逢吉知之。

translations.literal: Song's two younger brothers Yu and [㠖], drunk and witless, in cups with the sons of Yang Bin and Su Fengji sometimes spoke of having our residence seized; Fengji learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Song's younger brothers Yu and [㠖] were drunken and foolish. Over wine with the sons of Yang Bin and Su Fengji they would complain that their home had been taken, and Fengji heard of it.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·陶蒨傳》：李崧以宅券獻逢吉，逢吉不悅，而崧子弟數出怨言，崧懼，移疾不出。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Tao Qian: Li Song presented the house deed to Fengji; Fengji was displeased, while Song's sons and nephews often uttered resentful words; Song feared this and pleaded illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Tao Qian: Li Song offered Fengji the deed to his house. Fengji took offense, and Song's kin repeatedly voiced grievances. Song grew afraid, pleaded illness, and stopped attending court.

sentences.zh: 崧族子昉，嘗往候崧，崧語昉曰：「邇來朝廷於我有何議？

translations.literal: Song's clansman nephew Fang once went to visit Song; Song said to Fang: "Lately what talk has the court had about me?"
translations.idiomatic: Song's nephew Fang once called on him. Song asked, "What is the court saying about me these days?"

sentences.zh: 」昉曰：「無他，聞唯陶給事往往於稠人中厚誣叔父。

translations.literal: " Fang said, "Nothing else—I hear only that Attendant Tao Qian often slanders my uncle heavily in crowded gatherings."
translations.idiomatic: " Fang replied, "Nothing else—only that Attendant Tao Qian keeps slandering you loudly in public gatherings."

sentences.zh: 」崧嘆曰：「蒨自單州判官，吾取為集賢校理，不數年擢掌詔命，吾何負於陶氏子哉！

translations.literal: " Song sighed and said, "Qian was only a judge of Shan Prefecture; I took him as collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and within a few years promoted him to handle edicts—what have I done wrong to Tao's son!"
translations.idiomatic: " Song sighed, "Qian was only a prefectural judge when I brought him into the Hall of Assembled Worthies and within a few years put him in charge of edicts. What did I ever do to deserve this from Tao's protégé?"

sentences.zh: 」及崧遇禍，昉嘗因公事詣蒨，蒨問昉：「識李侍郎否？

translations.literal: " When Song met disaster, Fang once went to Qian on official business; Qian asked Fang: "Do you know Vice Director Li?"
translations.idiomatic: " After Song's fall, Fang once visited Qian on official business. Qian asked, "Do you know Vice Director Li?"

sentences.zh: 」昉斂衽應曰：「遠從叔耳。

translations.literal: " Fang straightened his robe and answered, "He is my distant uncle."
translations.idiomatic: " Fang straightened his robes and said, "He is my distant uncle."

sentences.zh: 」蒨曰：「李氏之禍，蒨出力焉。

translations.literal: " Qian said, "In the Li family's disaster, Qian exerted force."
translations.idiomatic: " Qian said, "I had a hand in the Li family's ruin."

sentences.zh: 」昉聞之汗出。）〉

translations.literal: " Fang, hearing this, broke into a sweat.))
translations.idiomatic: " Fang broke into a cold sweat on hearing this.))

sentences.zh: 有部曲葛延遇者，逋李嶼船傭，嶼撻之，督其所負，遇有同輩李澄亦事逢吉，葛延遇夜寄宿於澄家，以嶼見督情告，遂一夕同謀告變。

translations.literal: There was a retainer Ge Yanyu who defaulted on boat hire owed to Li Yu; Yu flogged him and pressed what was owed; Yanyu had a comrade Li Cheng who also served Fengji; Ge Yanyu lodged at Cheng's house by night and told of being pressed by Yu; in one night they jointly plotted to report a mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: A retainer named Ge Yanyu owed Li Yu money for boat hire. Yu beat him and demanded payment. Yanyu had a fellow named Li Cheng who also worked for Fengji. One night Yanyu stayed at Cheng's house and told him how Yu had hounded him. That night the two conspired to lodge a treason accusation.

sentences.zh: 逢吉覽狀示史宏肇，其日逢吉遣吏召崧至第，從容語及葛延遇告變之事，崧以幼女為托，逢吉遣吏送於侍衛獄。

translations.literal: Fengji read the report and showed it to Shi Hongzhao; that day Fengji sent clerks to summon Song to his residence, calmly speaking of Ge Yanyu's report of mutiny; Song entrusted his young daughter; Fengji sent clerks to deliver him to the guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji reviewed the accusation and showed it to Shi Hongzhao. That day he summoned Song to his mansion and calmly mentioned Ge Yanyu's charge. Song begged him to look after his young daughter. Fengji had him sent to the guard prison.

sentences.zh: 既行，崧恚曰：「自古未有不亡之國，不死之人。

translations.literal: As he went, Song said in anger: "Since antiquity there has never been a state that did not perish, nor a man who did not die."
translations.idiomatic: As he was led away, Song said bitterly, "Since antiquity no state has endured forever, and no man has escaped death."

sentences.zh: 」及為吏所鞫，乃自誣伏罪，舉家遇害，少長悉屍於市，人士冤之。

translations.literal: " When examined by officials, he then falsely confessed guilt; the whole family suffered disaster, young and old all corpses in the market; gentlemen deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: " Under interrogation he confessed to crimes he had not committed. His entire family was executed, bodies of every age left in the marketplace, and scholars across the realm regarded it as a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·王溥傳》：世宗嘗問：「漢相李崧蠟彈書結契丹，有記其詞者否？

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Wang Pu: Emperor Shizong once asked: "Did Han chancellor Li Song use a wax-sealed letter to ally with the Khitan—is there a record of its wording?"
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Wang Pu: Emperor Shizong once asked whether there was any record of the wording of a wax-sealed letter in which Han Chancellor Li Song had sought an alliance with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 」溥曰：「崧有此，肯示人耶？

translations.literal: " Pu said, "If Song had such a thing, would he show it to others?"
translations.idiomatic: " Pu replied, "If Song had done such a thing, would he have let anyone see it?"

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉輩陷之爾。

translations.literal: Su Fengji and his sort framed him, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji and his faction framed him—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」世宗遂優贈崧官。）〉

translations.literal: " Shizong then graciously posthumously ennobled Song.))
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then posthumously restored Song's honors.))

sentences.zh: 崧與徐臺符同學相善，乾祐三年秋，臺符夢崧謂曰：「予之冤橫，得請於帝矣。

translations.literal: Song and Xu Taifu had studied together and were close; in autumn of the third year of Qianyou, Taifu dreamed Song saying: "My wrongful suffering—I have obtained the Emperor's grant."
translations.idiomatic: Song and Xu Taifu had been classmates and close friends. In the autumn of the third year of Qianyou, Taifu dreamed that Song told him, "My grievous wrong has been heard in Heaven."

sentences.zh: 」及蘇、史之誅，並梟首於市，當崧所誅之地。

translations.literal: " When Su and Shi were executed, all were beheaded and displayed in the market at the place where Song had been executed.
translations.idiomatic: " When Su and Shi were put to death, their heads were displayed in the marketplace at the very spot where Song had been executed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，葛延遇、李澄亦以戮死。

translations.literal: Before long Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng also died by execution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Ge Yanyu and Li Cheng were executed as well.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李昉傳》：晉侍中崧，與昉同宗且同里，時人謂崧為「東李家」，昉為「西李」。

translations.literal: (Song History, Biography of Li Fang: Jin attendant-in-waiting Song and Fang were of the same clan and same district; people of the time called Song "the eastern Li family" and Fang "the western Li."
translations.idiomatic: (Song History, Biography of Li Fang: Jin Attendant-in-Waiting Song and Fang were kinsmen from the same hometown. People called Song's branch the Eastern Li and Fang's the Western Li.

sentences.zh: 漢末，崧被誅，至宋，其子璨自蘇州常熟縣令赴調，昉為訟其父冤，且言周太祖已為昭雪，贈官，還其田宅，錄璨而官之。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, Song was executed; by Song times his son Can came from magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to take assignment; Fang pleaded his father's injustice and also said Zhou Taizu had already cleared his name, granted posthumous office, returned his fields and house, and enrolled Can in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Han, Song was executed. Under the Song, his son Can traveled from his post as magistrate of Changshu in Suzhou to take up a new appointment. Fang pleaded his kinsman's innocence, noting that Taizu of Zhou had already cleared Song's name, restored his offices posthumously, returned his property, and secured an appointment for Can.

sentences.zh: 然璨幾五十，尚淹州縣之職。

translations.literal: Yet Can was nearly fifty and still stuck in prefectural and county posts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Can was nearly fifty and still languished in local posts.

sentences.zh: 詔授璨著作佐郎，後官至資善大夫。）〉

translations.literal: An edict appointed Can assistant editorial director; he later reached the office of Grand Master of the Palace for Venerating Goodness.))
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Can Assistant Editorial Director, and he eventually rose to Grand Master of the Palace for Venerating Goodness.))

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉，長安人。

translations.literal: Su Fengji was a native of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji was from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 父悅，逢吉母早喪，而悅鰥居，旁無侍者。

translations.literal: His father Yue—Fengji's mother died early, and Yue lived as a widower with no attendants at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue had lost Fengji's mother early and lived alone as a widower without anyone to wait on him.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，雖所飲不多，然漱醪終日。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine; though he did not drink much, he rinsed with ale all day.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine. Though he drank little at a sitting, he kept a cup at his lips from morning to night.

sentences.zh: 他人供膳，皆不稱旨，俟逢吉庖炙，方肯下箸。

translations.literal: Meals others provided never pleased him; he waited for Fengji's cooking before he would take chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Food prepared by anyone else never suited him. He would eat only after Fengji had cooked.

sentences.zh: 悅初仕蜀，官升朝列，逢吉初學為文，嘗代父染翰。

translations.literal: Yue first served Shu and rose to court rank; Fengji first studied writing and once drafted for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had begun his career in Shu and risen to court rank. Fengji was learning to write and sometimes drafted documents for his father.

sentences.zh: 悅嘗為高祖從事，甚見禮遇，因從容薦逢吉曰：「老夫耄矣，才器無取。

translations.literal: Yue had once been an aide to Gaozu and was greatly honored; he therefore casually recommended Fengji, saying: "This old man is aged; his talent has nothing to take."
translations.idiomatic: Yue had served Gaozu as an aide and was treated with great respect. He took occasion to recommend Fengji, saying, "I am old now and have no talent worth mentioning."

sentences.zh: 男逢吉粗學援毫，性復恭恪，如公不以犭屯犬之微，願令事左右。

translations.literal: My son Fengji has rough learning in wielding the brush and a nature again respectful and earnest; if Your Lordship does not disdain this humble cur's slight worth, I wish him to serve at your side.
translations.idiomatic: My son Fengji has some schooling in letters and a respectful disposition. If Your Lordship would not disdain this humble man's slight gift, I beg you to let him serve at your side.

sentences.zh: 」高祖召見，以神精爽惠，甚憐之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu summoned him for audience, finding his spirit bright and clever, and greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu received him and, finding him quick-witted and alert, took a strong liking to him.

sentences.zh: 有頃，擢為賓佐，凡有謀議，立侍其側。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to guest aide; whenever there was counsel he stood attending at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to staff adviser and stood at Gaozu's side whenever plans were discussed.

sentences.zh: 高祖素嚴毅，及鎮太原，位望崇重，從事稀得謁見，惟逢吉日侍左右。

translations.literal: Gaozu was by nature stern and resolute; when he secured Taiyuan his position and prestige were lofty, and aides rarely gained audience—only Fengji daily attended left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was stern by nature. Once he held Taiyuan his stature was immense, and staff members seldom gained an audience—only Fengji attended him every day.

sentences.zh: 兩使文簿，堆案盈幾，左右不敢輒通，逢吉置於懷袖，俟其悅色則諮之，多見其可。

translations.literal: Documents from both commissioners piled cases full on desks; attendants dared not casually pass them through; Fengji placed them in his bosom and sleeve, waited until Gaozu's expression was pleased then consulted him, and mostly won approval.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials from both commissioners piled the desks high, and attendants dared not pass them through. Fengji tucked them into his robe and waited until Gaozu was in good humor before raising them. Most were approved.

sentences.zh: 高祖建號於太原，逢吉自節度判官拜同平章事、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: When Gaozu established his title at Taiyuan, Fengji from military commissioner judge was appointed fellow Grand Councillor and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu proclaimed his reign at Taiyuan, Fengji rose from military commissioner judge to Grand Councillor and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 車駕至汴，朝廷百司庶務，逢吉以為己任，參決處置，並出胸臆，雖有當有否，而事無留滯。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bian, the hundred offices and myriad affairs of court—Fengji took them as his charge; participating in decisions and dispositions, all issued from his breast; though some were right and some wrong, matters had no delay.
translations.idiomatic: When the court reached Bianliang, Fengji took charge of the myriad affairs of government. Decisions poured from his own judgment. Some were wise and some were not, but nothing sat idle on his desk.

sentences.zh: 會翰林學士李濤從容侍帝，言及霸府二相，官秩未崇，逢吉旋加吏部尚書，未幾，轉左僕射，監修國史。

translations.literal: When Hanlin academician Li Tao calmly attended the Emperor and spoke of the two chancellors of the hegemon's residence whose ranks were not yet lofty, Fengji was soon given Minister of Personnel; before long he was transferred to Left Vice Director and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Li Tao remarked in passing that the two chancellors from Gaozu's former headquarters still held modest ranks. Fengji was promptly made Minister of Personnel, then soon Left Vice Director with charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 從征杜重威於鄴下，數乘醉抵辱周太祖。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye, he several times while drunk insulted the Zhou Founder.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye, he repeatedly insulted the future Zhou Founder while drunk.

sentences.zh: 及高祖大漸，與楊邠、史宏肇等臥內同受顧命。

translations.literal: When Gaozu grew gravely ill, with Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others he received the final charge within the bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu lay dying, he received the final imperial charge alongside Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and others at the bedside.

sentences.zh: 李濤與逢吉論甥舅之契，相得甚歡，濤之入相，逢吉甚有力焉。

translations.literal: Li Tao and Fengji were linked by nephew and uncle-in-law ties and got on very well; Tao's entering the chancellorship had Fengji's strong effort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao and Fengji were related by marriage and were on excellent terms. Fengji had done much to secure Tao's appointment as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 會濤上章，請出兩樞密為方鎮，帝怒，罷濤相，勒歸私第，時論疑濤承逢吉之風旨。

translations.literal: When Tao submitted a memorial asking to send the two military commissioners out as regional governors, the Emperor was angry, removed Tao from the chancellorship, and ordered him back to his private residence; opinion of the time suspected Tao carried Fengji's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao memorialized asking that the two military commissioners be sent out as regional governors, the Emperor was furious, stripped him of the chancellorship, and sent him home. Many suspected the memorial reflected Fengji's wishes.

sentences.zh: 先是，高祖踐阼之後，逢吉與蘇禹珪俱在中書，有所除拜，多違舊制，用舍升降，率意任情，至有自白丁而升宦路、由流外而除令錄者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Gaozu ascended the throne, Fengji and Su Yugui were both in the Secretariat; appointments and dismissals often violated old regulations; employment and dismissal, promotion and demotion followed whim and mood, until some rose from commoner status into the official path and from outside the flow were made magistrates and registrars—countless.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Gaozu took the throne, Fengji and Su Yugui controlled appointments from the Secretariat. They routinely ignored precedent, promoting and demoting at whim. Commoners were elevated to office and men from irregular backgrounds were made magistrates and registrars beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 物論紛然。

translations.literal: Public opinion was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion was in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 高祖方倚信二相，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: Gaozu was just then relying on and trusting the two chancellors; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu still trusted the two chancellors completely, and no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 逢吉尤貪財貨，無所顧避，求進之士，稍有物力者，即遣人微露風旨，許以美秩。

translations.literal: Fengji especially coveted goods and wealth without scruple; seekers of advancement who had even slight material means—he at once sent men to subtly reveal his intent and promised fine ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was especially greedy and shameless about it. Any office seeker with even modest wealth would receive a subtle hint that a handsome post could be arranged.

sentences.zh: 及楊邠為相，稍奪二蘇之權，自是盡斂手而已。

translations.literal: When Yang Bin became chancellor, he slightly stripped the two Sus of power; from then on they completely held their hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Bin became chancellor he gradually stripped the two Su ministers of power, and from then on they kept their hands to themselves.

sentences.zh: 邠每懲二蘇之失，艱於除拜，至於諸司補吏，與門胄出身，一切停罷。

translations.literal: Bin each time punished the two Su ministers' faults, making appointments difficult; as for clerks appointed in the various offices and men entering through gate and pedigree, all were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin repeatedly rebuked the two Su ministers and made appointments difficult. Clerical posts in every office and promotions through family connections were halted entirely.

sentences.zh: 時論以邠之蔽，固亦由逢吉、禹珪本不能至公於物之所致也。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time blamed Bin's narrowness, yet it also stemmed from Fengji and Yugui originally being unable to be fully fair toward things.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion blamed Yang Bin's narrowness, but it also reflected that Fengji and Yugui had never been fair in the first place.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖至汴，以故相馮道、李崧為契丹所俘，佇於真定，乃以崧第賜逢吉，道第賜禹珪，崧於西洛有別業，亦為逢吉所有。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu reached Bian, former chancellors Feng Dao and Li Song had been captured by the Khitan and detained at Zhending; Song's residence was bestowed on Fengji, Dao's on Yugui; Song also had a separate estate in western Luo, likewise taken by Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first reached Bianliang, former chancellors Feng Dao and Li Song were still Khitan captives at Zhending. Song's mansion was given to Fengji and Dao's to Yugui, and Song's estate in western Luoyang went to Fengji as well.

sentences.zh: 及真定逐契丹，崧、道歸朝，崧弟嶼以逢吉占據其第，時出怨言。

translations.literal: When Zhending drove out the Khitan, Song and Dao returned to court; Song's brother Yu, because Fengji occupied their residence, sometimes uttered resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhending expelled the Khitan, Song and Dao returned. Song's brother Yu complained that Fengji had seized their home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崧以西京宅券獻於逢吉，不悅。

translations.literal: Before long Song presented the western capital house deed to Fengji, who was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Song offered Fengji the deed to his Luoyang property, to Fengji's displeasure.

sentences.zh: 會崧有仆夫欲誣告謀反，逢吉誘致其狀，即告史宏肇，令逮捕其家。

translations.literal: It happened that Song had a servant who wished to lodge a false charge of rebellion; Fengji induced and obtained his statement, at once informed Shi Hongzhao, and ordered the arrest of his household.
translations.idiomatic: A servant of Song's tried to frame him for treason. Fengji coaxed out a written accusation, reported it to Shi Hongzhao, and ordered Song's family arrested.

sentences.zh: 逢吉遣直省吏召崧至第，即令監至侍衛獄。

translations.literal: Fengji sent a direct secretariat clerk to summon Song to his residence and at once had him escorted to the guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji sent a clerk to summon Song to his mansion and had him taken straight to the guard prison.

sentences.zh: 翌日，所司以獄辭上，其李嶼款招云：「與兄崧、弟鳷，與家僮二十人商議，比至山陵發引之時，同放火謀亂，其告是實。

translations.literal: The next day the responsible office submitted the prison statement; Li Yu's full confession said: "With elder brother Song and younger brother Zhi, with twenty household servants we discussed that when the imperial tomb procession departs we would together set fires and plot disorder—the report is true."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the court received the confession. Li Yu stated that he, his brother Song, his brother Zhi, and twenty servants had plotted to set fires and rebel when the imperial funeral procession departed.

sentences.zh: 」蓋自誣之辭也。

translations.literal: " This was plainly self-incriminating words.
translations.idiomatic: " It was plainly a forced confession.

sentences.zh: 逢吉仍以筆添註「二十人」字為「五十人」，封下有司，盡誅崧家。

translations.literal: Fengji still with his brush altered the characters "twenty men" to "fifty men," sealed and sent down to the offices, and executed Song's entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji altered "twenty men" to "fifty men" in the document, sealed it, and sent it down. Song's entire family was executed.

sentences.zh: 時人冤之，歸咎於逢吉。

translations.literal: People of the time deemed it unjust and blamed Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: The public regarded it as a gross injustice and blamed Fengji.

sentences.zh: 逢吉深文好殺，從高祖在太原時，嘗因事，高祖命逢吉靜獄，以祈福祐，逢吉盡殺禁囚以報。

translations.literal: Fengji loved harsh statutes and killing; when he followed Gaozu at Taiyuan, on one occasion Gaozu ordered Fengji to quiet the prisons to seek blessing and protection; Fengji killed all imprisoned convicts to report completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji loved harsh laws and bloodshed. Once at Taiyuan, Gaozu ordered him to clear the prisons as a blessing rite. Fengji executed every prisoner and reported the task done.

sentences.zh: 及執朝政，尤愛刑戮。

translations.literal: When he held court governance he especially loved punishments and executions.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he was especially fond of executions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患諸處盜賊，遣使捕逐，逢吉自草詔意云：「應有賊盜，其本家及四鄰同保人，並仰所在全族處斬。

translations.literal: The court was troubled by bandits everywhere and sent envoys to pursue them; Fengji himself drafted edict intent saying: "Wherever there are bandits, their original families and the four neighboring mutual-guarantee households—all are ordered by local authorities to execute the entire clans."
translations.idiomatic: The court struggled with banditry and sent agents to hunt thieves down. Fengji drafted an edict stating that wherever bandits were found, their families and four neighboring guarantor households were to be executed in full by local authorities.

sentences.zh: 」或謂逢吉曰：「為盜者族誅，猶非王法，鄰保同罪，不亦甚乎？

translations.literal: " Someone said to Fengji: "Executing the clan of a thief is still not royal law; making mutual-guarantee neighbors share guilt—is that not excessive?"
translations.idiomatic: " Someone told Fengji, "Clan punishment for theft is already beyond the law. Punishing guarantor neighbors as well—is that not extreme?"

sentences.zh: 」逢吉堅以為是，竟去「全族」二字。

translations.literal: " Fengji firmly held himself right and in the end removed the two characters "entire clan."
translations.idiomatic: " Fengji insisted he was right and finally struck the words "entire clan" from the edict.

sentences.zh: 時有鄆州捕賊使臣張令柔盡殺平陰縣十七村民，良由此也。

translations.literal: At the time Yanzhou bandit-catching envoy Zhang Lingrou entirely killed seventeen village people of Pingyin County—indeed from this.
translations.idiomatic: It was on this basis that Zhang Lingrou, the Yanzhou bandit-hunting envoy, massacred seventeen villagers in Pingyin County.

sentences.zh: 逢吉性侈靡，好鮮衣美食，中書供膳，鄙而不食，私庖供饌，務盡甘珍。

translations.literal: Fengji's nature was extravagant; he loved fresh clothes and fine food; Secretariat provisions he despised and would not eat; his private kitchen supplied meals striving for full sweetness and delicacy.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was extravagant and loved fine clothes and food. He refused the Secretariat's meals and had his private kitchen prepare only the richest delicacies.

sentences.zh: 嘗於私第大張酒樂以召權貴，所費千餘緡。

translations.literal: He once at his private residence greatly spread wine and music to summon the powerful, spending more than a thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He once hosted a lavish feast for the powerful at his mansion, spending more than a thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 其妻武氏卒，葬送甚盛，班行官及外州節制，有與逢吉相款洽者，皆令賫送綾羅絹帛，以備縞素。

translations.literal: When his wife the Lady Wu died, burial and send-off were very grand; ranked officials and outer prefecture commissioners who were on friendly terms with Fengji were all ordered to present silk and gauze for mourning white.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Wu died, the funeral was lavish. Every official and regional commissioner on good terms with Fengji was ordered to send silk for mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 失禮違度，一至如此。

translations.literal: Loss of ritual and violation of measure reached such a point.
translations.idiomatic: His breaches of ritual and propriety went that far.

sentences.zh: 又性不拘名教，繼母死不行服，妻死未周，其子並授官秩。

translations.literal: Moreover his nature did not bind to name and teaching: when his stepmother died he did not observe mourning; before his wife's mourning year was complete, his sons were all granted official ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He also scorned ritual propriety. He did not mourn his stepmother, and before his wife's mourning year ended he secured official posts for his sons.

sentences.zh: 有庶兄自外至，不白逢吉，便見諸子，逢吉怒，且懼他日淩弱其子息，乃密白高祖，誣以他事杖殺之。

translations.literal: A half-brother came from outside, did not inform Fengji, and at once saw the sons; Fengji was angry and also feared that in future he might bully his children; he secretly reported to Gaozu and on a false charge had him beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: A half-brother arrived from abroad and visited Fengji's sons without informing him. Fengji was furious and feared the man might one day threaten his children. He secretly accused him to Gaozu on false charges and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年秋，加守司空。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qianyou he was given acting Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Qianyou he was made acting Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 周太祖之將鎮鄴也，逢吉奏請落樞密使，隱帝曰：「有前例否？

translations.literal: When the Zhou Founder was about to secure Ye, Fengji memorialized asking to remove the military affairs commissioner post; the Hidden Emperor said: "Is there a precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: When the future Zhou Founder was to take command at Ye, Fengji asked that he be relieved of the military affairs commission. The Hidden Emperor asked whether there was precedent.

sentences.zh: 」逢吉奏曰：「樞密之任，方鎮帶之非便。

translations.literal: " Fengji memorialized: "The duty of military affairs—a regional commander holding it is not convenient."
translations.idiomatic: " Fengji replied, "A regional commander should not also hold the military affairs commission."

sentences.zh: 」史宏肇曰：「兼帶樞密，所冀諸軍稟畏。

translations.literal: " Shi Hongzhao said: "Concurrently holding military affairs is what we hope will make the armies stand in awe."
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Hongzhao said, "Keeping the commission will make the armies fear him."

sentences.zh: 」竟從宏肇之議。

translations.literal: " In the end they followed Hongzhao's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The court adopted Hongzhao's view.

sentences.zh: 宏肇怨逢吉之異己，逢吉曰：「此國家之事也，且以內制外則順，以外制內豈得便耶！

translations.literal: Hongzhao resented Fengji's differing from him; Fengji said: "This is the state's affair; moreover, inner controlling outer is fitting—outer controlling inner, how could that be convenient!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao resented Fengji's opposition. Fengji said, "This concerns the state. Inner authority over outer is proper; how can outer authority over inner be right?"

sentences.zh: 」事雖不從，物議多之。

translations.literal: " Though the matter was not followed, public opinion largely approved him.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he did not prevail, public opinion sided with him.

sentences.zh: 居無何，王章張飲，會逢吉與史宏肇有謔言，大為宏肇所詬，逢吉不校，幾至毆擊，逢吉馳馬而歸，自是將相失歡。

translations.literal: Before long, at Wang Zhang's open drinking, Fengji and Shi Hongzhao exchanged banter and were greatly reviled by Hongzhao; Fengji did not contend, nearly reaching blows; Fengji galloped home on horseback—from then on chancellor and commissioner lost harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Soon at Wang Zhang's banquet, Fengji and Shi Hongzhao traded barbs. Hongzhao berated him fiercely. Fengji held his tongue until blows nearly followed, then rode home. From then on the chancellor and the commissioner were estranged.

sentences.zh: 逢吉欲希外任，以紓宏肇之怒，既而中輟。

translations.literal: Fengji wished to hope for an outside post to ease Hongzhao's anger, but then stopped midway.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji hoped for a provincial post to appease Hongzhao, but soon abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，逢吉曰：「茍領一方鎮，只消得史公一處分。

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, Fengji said: "If I merely received one frontier command, it would take only one disposition from Lord Shi."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Fengji said, "If I took a frontier command, Lord Shi could destroy me with a single order."

sentences.zh: 則為齏粉矣。

translations.literal: Then I would become powder.
translations.idiomatic: I would be reduced to dust.

sentences.zh: 」李業輩惡宏肇、楊邠等，逢吉知之，每見業等，即微以言激怒之。

translations.literal: " Li Ye and his sort hated Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and others; Fengji knew this, and whenever he saw Ye and the rest he subtly used words to inflame them.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ye and his faction hated Hongzhao and Yang Bin. Fengji knew it and subtly goaded them whenever they met.

sentences.zh: 及宏肇等被害，逢吉不預其謀，聞變驚駭，即受宣徽，權知樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Hongzhao and others were killed, Fengji had not joined their plot; hearing the change he was shocked and alarmed, and at once received the Xuanhui commission and acted as military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzhao and the others were killed, Fengji had not been in on the plot. He was terrified at the news, took the Xuanhui post, and acted as military affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋令草制正授，制入，聞鄴兵至澶州乃止。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to draft the edict for formal appointment; when the edict entered, hearing Ye troops had reached Chun Prefecture it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to draft the formal appointment edict, but when Ye's army reached Chunzhou the edict was halted.

sentences.zh: 事急，逢吉謂人曰：「蕭墻之變，太覺匆遽，主上若有一言見問，必不至是矣。

translations.literal: As matters grew urgent, Fengji told people: "This trouble within the courtyard wall feels too hurried; if the sovereign had one word to ask me, it surely would not have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: As crisis mounted, Fengji said, "This palace coup came too fast. If the Emperor had asked my counsel, it would never have come to this."

sentences.zh: 」數夕宿於金祥殿之東，謂天官正王處訥曰：「夜來就枕未瞑，已見李崧在傍，生人與死人相接，無吉事也。

translations.literal: " For several nights he lodged east of the Jinxian Hall and told the chief astrologer Wang Chuna: "Last night as I lay down I had not closed my eyes when I already saw Li Song at my side—the living and the dead meeting, no auspicious matter."
translations.idiomatic: " For several nights he stayed east of the Jinxian Hall and told Chief Astrologer Wang Chuna, "Last night before I could sleep I saw Li Song beside me. When the living meet the dead, nothing good can come of it."

sentences.zh: 」及周太祖自鄴至汴，官軍敗於劉子陂，是夕逢吉宿於七里郊，與同舍痛飲，醉將自刎，左右止之。

translations.literal: " When the Zhou Founder came from Ye to Bian, the imperial army was defeated at Liuzi Slope; that evening Fengji lodged at Qili suburb, drank heavily with his roommate, drunk was about to cut his own throat, and attendants stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Zhou Founder marched from Ye to Bianliang and the imperial army was routed at Liuzi Slope, Fengji spent the night at Qili suburb. He drank heavily with his companion, grew drunk, and tried to cut his throat before attendants stopped him.

sentences.zh: 至曙，與隱帝同抵民舍，遂自殺。

translations.literal: At dawn, together with the Hidden Emperor he reached a commoner's house, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he and the Hidden Emperor reached a farmhouse, where Fengji killed himself.

sentences.zh: 周太祖定京城，與聶文進等同梟於北市，釋其家族。

translations.literal: When the Zhou Founder secured the capital, he and Nie Wenjin and others were beheaded and displayed in the north market; their families were released.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou Founder took the capital, Fengji and Nie Wenjin were beheaded and displayed in the north market. Their families were spared.

sentences.zh: 其梟首之處，適當李崧冤死之地。

translations.literal: The place of their displayed heads happened to be where Li Song had died unjustly.
translations.idiomatic: The place where their heads were displayed was exactly where Li Song had been unjustly executed.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，詔就西京賜其子莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun, an edict at the western capital bestowed on each of his sons one estate residence.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun, an edict granted each of his sons an estate residence in the western capital.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：高祖在河東幕府，闕書記，朝廷除前進士丘廷敏為之，以高祖有異志，恐為所累，辭疾不赴，遂改蘇逢吉。

translations.literal: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu was in the Hedong headquarters staff, lacking a secretary; the court appointed former jinshi Qiu Tingmin, who, because Gaozu had irregular ambitions, feared being implicated, pleaded illness and did not go, and so it was changed to Su Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: (Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: Gaozu's Hedong staff lacked a secretary. The court appointed the former jinshi Qiu Tingmin, but Tingmin feared being tied to Gaozu's ambitions, pleaded illness, and declined. Su Fengji was appointed instead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，契丹南侵，高祖仗順而起，兵不血刃而天下定，逢吉以佐命功，自掌書記拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan invaded south; Gaozu rose relying on legitimacy; the army took the realm without blood on blades; Fengji by merit aiding the mandate rose from chief secretary to vice director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan invaded. Gaozu rose claiming legitimacy and took the realm almost without bloodshed. Fengji's service in establishing the dynasty won him promotion from chief secretary to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 逾年，廷敏始選授鳳翔麟遊縣令。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Tingmin was at last selected and appointed magistrate of Linyou in Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, Tingmin was finally appointed magistrate of Linyou in Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 過堂之日，逢吉戲之，且撫所坐椅子曰：「合是長官坐，何故讓與鄙夫耶？

translations.literal: On the day of passing the hall audience, Fengji teased him and, patting the chair he sat in, said: "This ought to be the senior official's seat—why yield it to a base fellow?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his court audience, Fengji teased him and patted his chair, saying, "This seat should be mine—why yield it to a nobody?"

sentences.zh: 」廷敏遂漸悚而退。）〉

translations.literal: " Tingmin then gradually withdrew in fear.))
translations.idiomatic: " Tingmin withdrew in dismay.))

sentences.zh: 李鏻，唐宗屬也。

translations.literal: Li Lin was of the Tang imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin was a member of the Tang imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 父洎，韶州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ji was prefect of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ji served as prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 伯父湯，咸通中為給事中。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Tang, in the Xiantong era served as attendant within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Tang served as attendant within the Yellow Gate during the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 懿宗除乳母楚國夫人婿為夏州刺史，湯封還制書，詔曰：「朕少失所親，若非楚國夫人鞠養，則無朕此身，雖非朝典，望卿放下，仍今後不得援以為例。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong appointed the wet nurse Lady of Chu state's son-in-law as prefect of Xia; Tang sealed and returned the edict document; the edict said: "I lost my parents young; if not for the Lady of Chu state's nurturing, I would not have this body—though it is not court statute, I hope you will set it down, and hereafter it must not be cited as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong appointed the wet nurse's son-in-law, Lady of Chu, as prefect of Xia. Tang sealed the edict and returned it. The Emperor wrote, "I lost my parents young. Without Lady of Chu's care I would not be alive. Though this breaks precedent, please set the edict aside and do not cite it again."

sentences.zh: 」湯乃奉詔，其諒直如此。

translations.literal: " Tang then obeyed the edict—such was his understanding and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: " Tang obeyed. Such was his integrity.

sentences.zh: 鏻少舉進士，累舉不第。

translations.literal: Lin in youth presented himself for jinshi and repeatedly failed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Lin took the jinshi examination in his youth but failed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 客遊河朔，稱清海軍掌書記，謁定州王處直，不見禮。

translations.literal: As a guest he traveled the north of the Yellow River, calling himself chief secretary of the Qinghai Army; he visited Ding Prefecture's Wang Chuzhi and was not shown courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled north as a guest, claiming to be chief secretary of the Qinghai Army. Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou received him without courtesy.

sentences.zh: 鏻即脫綠被緋，入常山謁要人李宏規，以宗姓請兄事之，由是得進。

translations.literal: Lin then removed green and wore scarlet, entered Changshan to visit the powerful man Li Honggui, and by clan surname asked to treat him as elder brother—thereby gaining advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Lin shed his green robes for scarlet, went to Changshan, and visited the powerful Li Honggui. Claiming kinship through the imperial surname, he asked to serve Honggui as an elder brother and thereby advanced.

sentences.zh: 趙王镕辟為從事，镕卒，復為王德明賓客。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Rong recruited him as aide; when Rong died, he again became guest of Wang Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong of Zhao made him an aide. After Rong's death he became a retainer of Wang Deming.

sentences.zh: 德明使鏻聘於唐莊宗，鏻密疏德明之罪，且言可圖之狀，莊宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Deming sent Lin on embassy to Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong; Lin secretly memorialized Deming's crimes and also stated conditions for taking him—Zhuangzong praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Deming sent Lin on a mission to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang. Lin secretly reported Deming's crimes and described how he might be overthrown. Zhuangzong was pleased.

sentences.zh: 及常山平，以鏻為霸府支使。

translations.literal: When Changshan was pacified, Lin was made branch commissioner of the hegemon's residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshan fell, Lin was made branch commissioner of the hegemon's staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容請於莊宗曰：「鏻有四子，請誅之。

translations.literal: He once calmly requested of Zhuangzong: "Lin has four sons—please execute them."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Zhuangzong calmly, "I have four sons. Please execute them."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗問其故，對曰：「此輩生於常山，稟勃亂之氣，不可留也。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong asked the reason; he answered: "These were born in Changshan and received the spirit of sudden disorder—they cannot be kept."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong asked why. He replied, "They were born in Changshan and carry its turbulent spirit. They cannot be kept."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗笑而止。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong laughed and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong laughed and refused.

sentences.zh: 同光初，授宗正卿，俄兼工部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed director of the imperial clan court, and soon also vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he was made Director of the Imperial Clan Court and soon Vice Minister of Works as well.

sentences.zh: 常山有唐啟運陵，鏻受富民李守恭賂，署為陵臺令，守恭暴橫，為長吏所訴，按之以聞，鏻左授司農少卿，削金紫，未幾，出為河府副使。

translations.literal: Changshan had the Tang Qiyun Mausoleum; Lin accepted a bribe from the wealthy man Li Shougong and appointed him tomb-platform magistrate; Shougong was violent and overbearing, was sued by senior officials, investigated and reported; Lin was demoted to vice minister of agriculture, stripped of gold and purple, and before long sent out as deputy commissioner of the Yellow River prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Changshan held the Tang Qiyun Mausoleum. Lin took a bribe from the wealthy Li Shougong and appointed him tomb keeper. Shougong abused his power until officials reported him. Lin was demoted to Vice Minister of Agriculture, stripped of his gold-and-purple insignia, and soon sent out as deputy commissioner on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，歷兵部、戶部侍郎，工部、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, he passed through vice ministries of war and revenue, and ministries of works and revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong succeeded, Lin served as Vice Minister of War and Revenue and then Minister of Works and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 長興中，以與明宗有舊，常貯入相之意，從容謂時相曰：「唐祚中興，宜敦敘宗室，才高者合居相位。

translations.literal: In Changxing, because he had old ties with Mingzong, he constantly stored intent to enter the chancellorship and calmly told the chancellors of the time: "The Tang mandate is reviving; the imperial clan ought to be warmly treated—those of high talent should hold the phase position."
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, drawing on his old ties to Mingzong, he constantly harbored hopes of becoming chancellor. He told the current chancellors, "The Tang house is reviving. The imperial clan should be honored, and the most capable should hold the highest office."

sentences.zh: 仆雖不才，曾事莊宗霸府，見今上於藩邸時。

translations.literal: I though lacking talent once served Zhuangzong's hegemon residence and saw the present sovereign in his princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: I may lack talent, but I served Zhuangzong's staff and knew the present Emperor when he was still a prince.

sentences.zh: 家代重侯累相，靖安李氏，不在諸族之下；

translations.literal: My house for generations held heavy marquisates and successive chancellorships; the Jing'an Li clan is not below the other clans;
translations.idiomatic: My family has produced marquises and chancellors for generations. The Jing'an Li are second to none among the clans;

sentences.zh: 論才較藝，何讓眾人。

translations.literal: in comparing talent and testing skill, why yield to the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: and in talent and accomplishment I yield to no one.

sentences.zh: 久置仆於朝行，諸君安乎？

translations.literal: Long placing me in court ranks—are you gentlemen at ease?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you leave me long in the lower ranks. Are you at ease with that?

sentences.zh: 」馮道、趙鳳每怒其僭。

translations.literal: " Feng Dao and Zhao Feng each grew angry at his presumption.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were furious at his presumption.

sentences.zh: 有頃，鏻因淮南細人言事，乃謂樞密使安重誨曰：「偽吳欲歸國久矣，若朝廷先遣使諭之，則旋踵而至矣。

translations.literal: Before long, because of a Huainan petty man's report on affairs, he told military affairs commissioner An Chonghui: "The false Wu has long wished to return to the realm; if the court first sends envoys to instruct them, they will arrive in a turn of the heel."
translations.idiomatic: Soon, based on word from a Huainan informant, he told Military Affairs Commissioner An Chonghui, "Wu has long wished to submit. If the court sends envoys first, they will come at once."

sentences.zh: 」重誨然之，以玉帶與細人，令往淮南為信，久而不反，由是出鏻為兗州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: " Chonghui approved this, gave a jade belt to the petty man, and ordered him to go to Huainan as messenger; long he did not return, and thereby Lin was sent out as marching secretary of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Chonghui agreed, gave the informant a jade belt, and sent him to Huainan as envoy. When he never returned, Lin was exiled as marching secretary at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 得代歸闕，復為戶部尚書，尋轉兵部尚書，有頃兼判太常卿事。

translations.literal: When relieved and returned to court, he again became minister of revenue; soon transferred to minister of war; before long also oversaw director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After his term ended he returned and was again Minister of Revenue, then Minister of War, and soon also oversaw the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嘗權典選部，銓綜失序，物論非之。

translations.literal: He once acted as head of the selection department; evaluation and ordering were disorderly, and public opinion criticized him.
translations.idiomatic: He once headed the selection office and handled appointments so badly that public opinion turned against him.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，守太子少保。

translations.literal: In Jin Tianfu he held acting Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Jin in the Tianfu era he served as acting Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開運中，遷太子太保。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun he was promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 高祖至闕，授守司徒，數月而卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached court he was given acting Minister of Education; several months later he died, age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached the capital, Lin was made acting Minister of Education. He died several months later at eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太傅。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 龍敏，字欲訥，幽州永清人。

translations.literal: Long Min, style Yune, was a native of Yongqing in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Long Min, styled Yune, was from Yongqing in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少學為儒，仕鄉里為假掾。

translations.literal: In youth he studied as a Confucian and served in his home district as acting clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics in youth and served his home district as acting clerk.

sentences.zh: 劉守光不道，敏避地浮陽，會戴思遠渡河而南，乃從之。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang was unprincipled; Min fled to Fuyang; it happened that Dai Siyuan crossed the river southward, and he followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang turned tyrannical, Min fled to Fuyang. When Dai Siyuan crossed the Yellow River south, Min followed him.

sentences.zh: 鄉人周知裕仕梁為裨將，敏往依焉，知裕屢薦不調，敏丐遊都邑累年。

translations.literal: His townsman Zhou Zhiyu served Liang as deputy general; Min went to rely on him; Zhiyu repeatedly recommended him without appointment; Min begged to wander the capital districts for many years.
translations.idiomatic: His townsman Zhou Zhiyu was a Liang deputy general. Min attached himself to Zhou, who recommended him repeatedly without success. Min wandered the capital for years seeking office.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗定魏博，敏聞故人馮道為霸府記室，乃客於河中，歲歸太原，館於馮道之家，監軍使張承業即署敏為巡官，典監軍奏記。

translations.literal: When Tang's Zhuangzong secured Weibo, Min heard his old acquaintance Feng Dao was recorder of the hegemon's residence; he sojourned at Hezhong, each year returning to Taiyuan and lodging at Feng Dao's home; military overseer Zhang Chengye at once appointed Min touring officer in charge of the overseer's memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong secured Weibo, Min learned that Feng Dao was on the hegemon's staff. He stayed at Hezhong and returned yearly to Taiyuan, lodging with Feng Dao. Military Overseer Zhang Chengye appointed him touring officer in charge of memorials.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平河、洛，征為司門員外郎，以家貧乏養，求為興唐少尹。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified the Yellow River region and Luoyang, he was summoned as outer vice director of the Gate Office; because his family was poor and lacked support, he requested to be junior prefect of Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took the Yellow River region and Luoyang, Min was summoned as Outer Vice Director of the Gate Office. Because his family was poor, he asked for the post of junior prefect of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，丁母喪，退居鄴下，會趙在禮據鄴城，以敏鄉人，強起令署事，又為亂軍所迫，敏不敢拒。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered mourning for his mother and retired to live below Ye; it happened that Zhao Zaili held Ye city; because Min was a townsman, he was forcibly raised to order him to handle affairs, and again was pressed by mutinous troops—Min dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he mourned his mother and retired to Ye. Zhao Zaili seized the city and, recognizing Min as a townsman, forced him into service. Mutinous troops also pressed him, and Min could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 明年，在禮鎮浮陽，敏復居喪制，服闋，除戶部郎中，改諫議大夫、御史中丞。

translations.literal: The next year Zaili secured Fuyang; Min again observed mourning regulations; when mourning ended he was made director in the Ministry of Revenue, then changed to remonstrance grandee and censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Zaili took Fuyang. Min resumed mourning. After the period ended he was made Director in the Ministry of Revenue, then Remonstrance Grandee and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時敏父鹹式年七十，鹹式之父年九十餘，供養二尊，朝夕無懈。

translations.literal: At the time Min's father Xianshi was seventy; Xianshi's father was over ninety; he supported both elders morning and evening without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Min's father Xianshi was seventy, and Xianshi's father was over ninety. Min cared for both elders morning and night without fail.

sentences.zh: 鹹式以敏貴，得秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: Xianshi because Min was honored was able to retire as director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Min's rank, Xianshi was allowed to retire as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敏為兵部侍郎，奉使幽州，鄉里耆舊留宴盡歡。

translations.literal: Min as vice minister of war was sent on mission to You Prefecture; elders of his home district detained him for feasts to full joy.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister of War, Min was sent on a mission to You Prefecture, where the elders of his hometown feasted him warmly.

sentences.zh: 馮赟為北京留守，奏敏為副，赟入掌樞密，敏為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Feng Yun was northern capital regent and memorialized Min as deputy; when Yun entered to hold military affairs, Min became vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun, regent of the northern capital, recommended Min as his deputy. When Feng took charge of military affairs, Min became Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 敏學術不甚長，然外柔而內剛，愛決斷大計。

translations.literal: Min's learning was not very deep, yet outwardly soft and inwardly firm, he loved deciding great plans.
translations.idiomatic: Min was not deeply learned, but though outwardly mild he was inwardly firm and loved to decide great matters.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，從唐末帝在懷州，時趙德鈞父子有異圖，晉安寨旦夕憂陷，末帝計無從出，問計於從臣。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai he followed the Last Emperor of Tang at Huai Prefecture; at the time Zhao Dejun and his son had irregular designs; the Jin'an camp feared capture morning and night; the Last Emperor had no plan to emerge and asked counsel of attending ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai he followed the Last Emperor of Tang at Huai Prefecture. Zhao Dejun and his son were plotting rebellion, and the Jin'an camp faced imminent collapse. The Emperor had no plan and asked his ministers for counsel.

sentences.zh: 敏奏曰：「臣有一計，請以援兵從東丹王李贊華取幽州路趨西樓，契丹主必有北顧之患。

translations.literal: Min memorialized: "Your servant has one plan—please take relief troops following Prince of Eastern Dan Li Zanhua by the Youzhou road toward Xilou; the Khitan ruler will surely have worry of looking north."
translations.idiomatic: Min proposed, "I have a plan. Send relief troops with Prince Li Zanhua of Eastern Dan along the Youzhou route toward Xilou. The Khitan ruler will have to look to his rear."

sentences.zh: 」末帝然之，而不能用。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor approved it but could not use it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Last Emperor agreed but could not act on it.

sentences.zh: 敏又謂末帝親將李懿曰：「君連姻帝戚，社稷之危，不俟翹足，安得默默茍全耶！

translations.literal: Min also told the Last Emperor's close general Li Yi: "Sir, you are joined in marriage to imperial kin—the realm's peril does not wait for lifting a foot—how can you silently seek mere preservation!"
translations.idiomatic: Min also told the Emperor's close general Li Yi, "You are kin to the throne by marriage. The realm's peril will not wait. How can you seek only to save yourself in silence?"

sentences.zh: 」懿因籌德鈞必破蕃軍之狀，敏曰：「仆燕人也，諳趙德鈞之為人，膽小謀拙，所長者守城寨、嬰壕塹、篤勵健兒耳！

translations.literal: " Yi then worked out how Dejun would surely break the barbarian army; Min said: "I am a man of Yan and know Zhao Dejun's character—timid in courage, clumsy in planning; what he excels at is holding fortresses and camps, hugging moats and ramparts, and earnestly rousing stout warriors!"
translations.idiomatic: " As Yi worked out how Dejun might defeat the Khitan army, Min said, "I am a Yan man and know Zhao Dejun well. He is timid and clumsy. He can hold forts, man ramparts, and drill soldiers—that is all."

sentences.zh: 若見大敵，奮不顧身，摧堅陷陣，必不能矣。

translations.literal: If he meets a great enemy, striving without regard for body, crushing hard positions and breaking formations—he surely cannot.
translations.idiomatic: But facing a great enemy, charging recklessly, and breaking enemy lines—he cannot do that.

sentences.zh: 況名位震主，奸以謀身乎！

translations.literal: Moreover his fame and position shook the sovereign—is he not treacherous in plotting for himself!
translations.idiomatic: And his stature already overshadows the throne—is he not scheming for himself?

sentences.zh: 仆有狂策，不知濟否，茍能必行，亦救寨之一術也。

translations.literal: I have a reckless plan, not knowing whether it will succeed; if it can surely be carried out, it is also one method to save the camp.
translations.idiomatic: I have a bold plan. I do not know whether it will work, but if it can be executed, it may yet save the camp.

sentences.zh: 」懿請言之，曰：「如聞駕前馬僅有五千匹，請於其間選壯馬精甲健夫千人，仆願與郎萬金二人

translations.literal: " Yi asked him to speak it; he said: "As I hear, before the imperial carriage there are only five thousand horses—please from among them select a thousand stout horses, fine armor, and strong men; I wish to go with Lang Wanjin, the two of us"
translations.idiomatic: " Yi asked him to explain. Min said, "I hear there are only five thousand horses with the imperial train. Choose a thousand strong mounts, fine armor, and hardy men. I wish to go with Lang Wanjin"

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：郎萬金為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Lang Wanjin was prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Lang Wanjin was prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 胡三省云：萬金，當時勇將也。）〉

translations.literal: Hu Sanxing says: Wanjin was a brave general of the time.))
translations.idiomatic: Hu Sanxing notes that Wanjin was a renowned warrior of the day.))

sentences.zh: 路出山，夜冒敵騎，循山入大寨，千騎之內，得其半濟，則寨無虞矣。

translations.literal: By a route out of the mountains, by night braving enemy cavalry, following the mountains into the great camp—within a thousand riders, if we get half across, then the camp will have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: By a mountain route, strike the enemy cavalry by night, and enter the great camp along the hills. If half of the thousand horsemen can cross, the camp will be secure.

sentences.zh: 張敬達等幽閉，不知朝廷援兵近遠，若知大軍在團柏谷中，雖鐵障亦可沖踏，況敵騎乎！

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda and others are shut in and do not know whether court relief troops are near or far; if they knew the great army is in Tuanbai Valley, even iron barriers could be charged and trampled—how much more enemy cavalry!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda and the others are trapped and do not know how near relief may be. If they knew a great army lay in Tuanbai Valley, even iron walls could be broken—let alone enemy cavalry!

sentences.zh: 」末帝聞之曰：「龍敏之心極壯，用之晚矣。

translations.literal: " The Last Emperor heard this and said: "Long Min's heart is extremely bold—he was employed too late."
translations.idiomatic: " The Last Emperor heard this and said, "Long Min's spirit is magnificent. We called on him too late."

sentences.zh: 」人亦以為大言，然其慷慨感激，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " People also regarded it as grand talk, yet his generous indignation was all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: " Others thought it boastful, yet his passionate boldness was always of this kind.

sentences.zh: 子袞，登進士第，文彩遒雋。

translations.literal: His son Gun passed the jinshi examination; his literary color was forceful and distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gun passed the jinshi examination and wrote with vigor and grace.

sentences.zh: 仕周為左拾遺、直史館，早卒。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as left remonstrance official and direct historian of the History Office, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Left Remonstrance Official and direct historian of the History Office, and died young.

sentences.zh: 張允，鎮州束鹿人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun was a native of Shulu in Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun was from Shulu in Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父徵。

translations.literal: His father was Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Zheng.

sentences.zh: 允幼學為儒，仕本州為參軍。

translations.literal: Yun in youth studied as a Confucian and served his prefecture as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Yun studied the classics in youth and served his home prefecture as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 張文禮之據州叛，莊宗致討，允隨文禮子處瑾請降於鄴，不許，與處瑾並系於獄。

translations.literal: When Zhang Wenli seized the prefecture in rebellion, Zhuangzong sent punishment; Yun followed Wenli's son Chujin to request surrender at Ye, was not permitted, and was imprisoned together with Chujin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wenli rebelled and seized the prefecture, Zhuangzong marched against him. Yun followed Wenli's son Chujin to offer surrender at Ye, was refused, and was imprisoned with Chujin.

sentences.zh: 鎮、冀平，宥之，留於鄴，署本府功曹。

translations.literal: When Zhen and Ji were pacified, he was pardoned, kept at Ye, and appointed merit officer of the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhen and Ji were pacified he was pardoned, remained at Ye, and was appointed merit officer of the prefectural staff.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮嬰城叛，署節度推官，從歷滄、兗二鎮書記，入為監察御史，歷右補闕、起居舍人，充宏文館直學士、水部員外郎、知制誥。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili held the city in rebellion, he was appointed military commissioner investigating officer; he followed through Cang and Yan as secretary, entered as investigating censor, passed through right remonstrance supplementer and attendant of the bedchamber, and filled posts as direct academician of the Hongwen Hall, outer vice director of water, and edict drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rebelled and held the city, Yun was made investigating officer on the military commissioner's staff. He served as secretary at Cang and Yan, then entered court as investigating censor, remonstrance supplementer, and attendant of the bedchamber, and became direct academician of the Hongwen Hall, Outer Vice Director of Water, and edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，皇子重美為河南尹，典六軍諸衛事，時朝廷選參佐，以允剛介，改給事中，充六軍判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Prince Chongmei was Henan intendant and oversaw the Six Armies and guard offices; at the time the court selected aides; because Yun was stern and upright, he was changed to attendant within the Yellow Gate and made judge of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai, Prince Chongmei of Henan oversaw the Six Armies and guard offices. The court chose aides for him. Because Yun was stern and upright, he was made Attendant within the Yellow Gate and judge of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 尋罷職，轉左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon his post was ended and he was transferred to left regular attendant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left that post and was made Left Regular Attendant of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，允以國朝頻有肆赦，乃進「駁赦論」，曰：「《管子》云：『凡赦者小利而大害，久而不勝其禍；

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu, because the dynasty frequently had general amnesties, Yun submitted a "Refutation of Amnesty," saying: "Guanzi says: 'Every amnesty brings small profit and great harm; in time one cannot overcome its calamity;'
translations.idiomatic: Early in Later Jin's Tianfu era, noting how often the court proclaimed general amnesties, Yun submitted a "Refutation of Amnesty," citing Guanzi: "Amnesties bring small gains and great harm; in time their harm cannot be overcome."

sentences.zh: 無赦者小害而大利，久而不勝其福。

translations.literal: 'No amnesty brings small harm and great profit; in time one cannot overcome its blessing.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Without amnesties there is small harm and great good; in time their good cannot be overcome."

sentences.zh: 』又《漢紀》云：『吳漢疾篤，帝問所欲言。

translations.literal: 'The Han Annals also says: "Wu Han was gravely ill; the Emperor asked what he wished to say.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Han Annals also records that when Wu Han lay dying, the Emperor asked his final counsel.

sentences.zh: 對曰：唯願陛下無為赦耳。

translations.literal: He answered: I only wish Your Majesty never to grant amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I only wish Your Majesty would never proclaim amnesties."

sentences.zh: 』如是者何？
