translations.literal: ' Why is this so?'"
translations.idiomatic: " Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 蓋行赦不以為恩，不行赦亦不以為無恩，為罰有罪故也。

translations.literal: Because granting amnesty is not taken as grace, and not granting amnesty is also not taken as lack of grace—it is because punishment is for the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Because amnesty is not true grace, and withholding amnesty is not cruelty—it is simply punishing the guilty.

sentences.zh: 竊觀自古帝王，皆以水旱則降德音而宥過，開狴牢以放囚，冀感天心以救其災者，非也。

translations.literal: I have observed that since antiquity emperors, whenever there was flood or drought, would issue gracious edicts and pardon faults, open prisons and release convicts, hoping to move Heaven's heart to save their disasters—this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that since antiquity, whenever flood or drought struck, emperors issued gracious edicts, pardoned offenders, and opened prisons hoping to move Heaven and end the disaster. This is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 假有二人訟，一有罪，一無罪，若有罪者見舍，則無罪者銜冤，銜冤者彼何疏，見舍者此何親乎？

translations.literal: Suppose two men sue: one guilty, one not; if the guilty one is pardoned, then the guiltless one harbors injustice—why is the wronged one distant, and why is the pardoned one close?
translations.idiomatic: Suppose two men go to law, one guilty and one innocent. If the guilty is pardoned, the innocent is wronged. Why favor the guilty and slight the innocent?

sentences.zh: 如此則是致災之道，非救災之術也。

translations.literal: In this way it is the path that brings disaster, not the method that saves from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That is a path to disaster, not a way to end it.

sentences.zh: 自此小民遇天災則喜，皆相勸為惡，曰國家好行赦，必赦我以救災，如此即是國家教民為惡也。

translations.literal: From this, when common people meet natural disasters they rejoice, each urging the other to do evil, saying the state loves to grant amnesty and will surely pardon us to save the disaster—in this way the state teaches the people to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: From then on commoners rejoice at disasters and urge one another to crime, saying the state loves amnesties and will surely pardon them to end the calamity. Thus the state teaches the people to do evil.

sentences.zh: 且天道福善禍淫，若以舍為惡之人，而便變災為福，則又是天助其惡民也。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven's way blesses the good and afflicts the licentious; if by pardoning evil men one turns disaster into blessing, then again Heaven is helping evil people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blesses the good and punishes the wicked. To pardon the wicked and call it ending disaster is to make Heaven aid evildoers.

sentences.zh: 細而論之，必不然矣。

translations.literal: Examined in detail, it surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Considered closely, that cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 儻或天降之災，蓋欲警誡人主。

translations.literal: If perhaps Heaven sends down disaster, it is likely to warn and admonish the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven sends disaster, it is likely to warn the ruler.

sentences.zh: 節嗜欲，務勤儉，恤鰥寡，正刑罰，不濫舍有罪，不僭殺無辜，使美化行於下，聖德聞於上，則雖有水旱，亦不為沴矣。

translations.literal: Restrain desires, strive for diligence and thrift, pity widows and orphans, rectify punishments, do not indiscriminately pardon the guilty, do not exceed in killing the innocent, let refined transformation proceed below and sagely virtue be heard above—then though there be flood and drought, they will not become baleful influences.
translations.idiomatic: Restrain desire, practice thrift, pity widows and orphans, enforce justice, pardon no guilty man rashly, kill no innocent man, let virtue spread below and sagely fame rise above—then even flood and drought will not become calamity.

sentences.zh: 豈以濫舍有罪，而反能救其災乎？

translations.literal: How can indiscriminately pardoning the guilty in turn save their disasters?
translations.idiomatic: How can rash pardons of the guilty save anyone from disaster?

sentences.zh: 彰其德乎？

translations.literal: Manifest their virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Or display their virtue?

sentences.zh: 是知赦之不可行也明哉！

translations.literal: Thus it is clear that amnesty must not be carried out!
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is clear that amnesties must not be practiced!

sentences.zh: 」帝覽而嘉之，降詔獎飾，仍付史館。

translations.literal: " The Emperor read it and praised it, issued an edict to reward and adorn him, and also delivered it to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor read it with approval, issued an edict praising him, and sent the essay to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷禮部侍郎，凡三典貢部，改御史中丞，轉兵部侍郎、知制誥，充翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was moved to vice minister of rites, thrice headed the tribute department, was changed to censor-in-chief, transferred to vice minister of war and edict drafter, and filled the post of Hanlin academician ex officio.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became Vice Minister of Rites, thrice headed the examination bureau, then Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of War, edict drafter, and Hanlin Academician Ex Officio.

sentences.zh: 契丹入京城，落職守本官。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the capital, he was reduced in office but kept his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital, he was demoted but kept his original rank.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·劉溫叟傳》：契丹入京師，溫叟懼隨契丹北徙，與承旨張允求去職。

translations.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Liu Wensou: When the Khitan entered the capital, Wensou feared following the Khitan northward and, with ex officio academician Zhang Yun, requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Liu Wensou: When the Khitan took the capital, Wensou feared being carried north with them and, with Academician Ex Officio Zhang Yun, asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒，欲黜為縣令。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was angry and wished to demote them to county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was furious and wished to demote them to county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽曰：「學士不稱職而求解者，罷之可也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said: "Academicians who do not fit their duties and seek release—dismissing them is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou said, "If academicians are unfit and ask to resign, dismissal is enough."

sentences.zh: 」得不黜。）〉

translations.literal: " They were not demoted.))
translations.idiomatic: " They were not demoted.))

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou he was made Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 自誅史宏肇後，京城士庶，連甍恐悚，允每朝退，即宿於相國寺僧舍。

translations.literal: After Shi Hongzhao was executed, the capital's gentry and commoners were in linked-roof terror; after each court session Yun lodged in the monk's quarters of Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hongzhao's execution the capital lived in fear. After each court session Yun slept in the monks' quarters at Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 及北軍入京師，允匿於佛殿藻井之上，墜屋而卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: When the northern army entered the capital, Yun hid above the coffered ceiling of the Buddha hall, fell through the roof, and died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern army entered the capital, Yun hid in the coffered ceiling of a Buddha hall, fell through the roof, and died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子鸞，仕皇朝為太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Luan served the imperial court as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan served the dynasty as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 任延皓，并州人也。

translations.literal: Ren Yanhao was a man of Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yanhao was from Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 業術數風雲之事。

translations.literal: He practiced the arts of calculation and omens of wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced divination and the reading of celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖在太原重圍時，高祖最為親要，延皓以本業請見，高祖甚加禮遇。

translations.literal: When Jin Gaozu was in heavy siege at Taiyuan, Yanhao was among those closest to him; Yanhao by his profession requested audience and Gaozu greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Jin was besieged at Taiyuan, Yanhao was among his closest confidants. Yanhao sought audience through his craft and was treated with great honor.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，延皓授太原掾，尋改交城、文水令，皆高祖慰薦之力也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin Tianfu, Yanhao was appointed Taiyuan clerk; soon changed to magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui—all through Gaozu's comforting recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu, Yanhao was made a Taiyuan clerk, then magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, all through Gaozu's patronage.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，延皓多言外事，出入無間，高祖左右皆憚之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured Taiyuan, Yanhao spoke much of outside affairs and came and went without interval; those at Gaozu's side all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, Yanhao spoke constantly of outside affairs and came and went freely. Everyone around Gaozu feared him.

sentences.zh: 在文水聚斂財賄，民欲陳訴，延皓知之。

translations.literal: At Wenshui he amassed wealth and bribes; the people wished to lodge complaints; Yanhao learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenshui he extorted wealth and bribes. When the people tried to complain, Yanhao learned of it.

sentences.zh: 一日，先誣告縣吏結集百姓，欲劫縣庫。

translations.literal: One day he first falsely reported that county clerks had gathered the people and intended to rob the county treasury.
translations.idiomatic: One day he preemptively accused the county clerks of rallying the people to raid the treasury.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，遣騎軍並擒縣民十數，族誅之，冤枉之聲，聞於行路。

translations.literal: Gaozu was angry, sent cavalry who together seized more than ten county people and executed their clans; cries of injustice were heard on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was enraged and sent cavalry who seized a dozen townspeople and executed their families. The cries of the wronged echoed along the roads.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，累官至殿中監，恃寵使氣，人望而畏之，雖宰輔之重，延皓視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, Yanhao rose by degrees to director of the palace bureau, relying on favor and throwing his weight; people looked at him in fear; even the weight of chancellors—Yanhao viewed them with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Yanhao rose to Director of the Palace Bureau. Arrogant with favor, he inspired fear and treated even chancellors with contempt.

sentences.zh: 劉崇在河東，日常切齒。

translations.literal: Liu Chong in Hedong daily gnashed his teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong in Hedong gnashed his teeth at him daily.

sentences.zh: 及魏王承訓薨，歸葬太原，令延皓擇葬地，時有山岡僧謂劉崇曰：「魏王葬地不吉，恐有重喪。

translations.literal: When Prince of Wei Chengxun died and was returned for burial at Taiyuan, Yanhao was ordered to choose the burial ground; at the time a hill monk told Liu Chong: "The Prince of Wei's burial ground is inauspicious—fear repeated mourning."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chengxun of Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan, Yanhao chose the site. A monk told Liu Chong, "The site is ill-omened. There may be further mourning."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，高祖崩，崇以僧言奏之，乃配流延皓於麟州。

translations.literal: " Before long Gaozu died; Chong memorialized the monk's words and then exiled Yanhao to Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Gaozu died. Chong reported the monk's words and had Yanhao exiled to Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 路由文水，市民擲瓦毆罵甚眾，吏人救之僅免。

translations.literal: The route passed Wenshui; townspeople threw tiles and cursed and beat him in great numbers; clerks saved him and he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Wenshui, townspeople pelted him with tiles and cursed him. Officials barely saved him from the mob.

sentences.zh: 既至貶所，劉崇令人殺之，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Once he reached the place of exile, Liu Chong sent men to kill him and confiscated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached exile, Liu Chong had him killed and his property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李崧仕唐、晉之兩朝，聳伊、臯之重望，考其器業，無忝臺衡。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Song served the two dynasties of Tang and Jin, towering with the heavy repute of Yi Yin and Gao Yao; examining his capacity and achievement, he did not disgrace the balance of state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Li Song served both Tang and Jin, bearing the stature of Yi Yin and Gao Yao. Judged by talent and achievement, he did not disgrace the highest office.

sentences.zh: 會多僻之朝，被參夷之戮，人之不幸，天亦難忱。

translations.literal: He met a time of many perverse courts and suffered execution by dismemberment—man's misfortune, and Heaven too is hard to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he met perverse times and died by dismemberment. Such is human misfortune; even Heaven is hard to trust.

sentences.zh: 逢吉秉蛇虺之心，竊夔、龍之位，殺人不忌，與國俱亡。

translations.literal: Fengji held the heart of serpent and viper, usurped the positions of Kui and Long, killed without scruple, and perished with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji harbored a viper's heart, usurped high office, killed without restraint, and perished with the state.

sentences.zh: 李崧之冤血未銷，逢吉之梟首斯至，冥報之事，安可忽諸！

translations.literal: Li Song's unjust blood had not dried when Fengji's displayed head arrived—matters of retribution in the dark realm, how can they be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Li Song's blood of injustice had scarcely dried when Fengji's head was displayed. Retribution in the unseen world—how can one ignore it!

sentences.zh: 自李鏻而下，凡數君子者，皆踐履朝行，彰施帝載，國華邦直，斯焉在哉！

translations.literal: From Li Lin downward, all several gentlemen trod the court ranks, displayed on the imperial record, national flower and state uprightness—here they are!
translations.idiomatic: From Li Lin onward, these several gentlemen walked the halls of court, served the throne, and embodied the nation's honor and integrity.

sentences.zh: 惟延皓之醜行，宜乎不得其死矣。

translations.literal: Only Yanhao's ugly conduct—fitting that he should not obtain a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanhao's vile conduct made his violent end fitting.
